text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until now.

versions.text: "Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you against Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until now.
versions.explanation: The preposition עַל here is best taken as 'concerning/about' since the scroll contained words of both judgment and hope regarding these peoples; 'against' narrows the sense unnecessarily.

text: Perhaps when the house of Judah hears of all the disaster I intend to bring on them, they will each turn from their evil way, and I will forgive their guilt and their sin."
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on the scroll all the words the LORD had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah instructed Baruch: "I am restricted; I cannot go to the house of the LORD.

So you go, and on a day of fasting read aloud from the scroll the words of the LORD that you wrote at my dictation. Read them in the hearing of the people at the house of the LORD, and in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.
Perhaps their plea for mercy will come before the LORD, and each of them will turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and wrath the LORD has pronounced against this people."
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, reading the words of the LORD from the scroll at the house of the LORD.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, a fast before the LORD was proclaimed for all the people of Jerusalem and for all who came in to Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.

Then, in the hearing of all the people, Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll at the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD read from the scroll,

he went down to the king's palace, to the chamber of the scribe, where all the officials were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah reported to them everything he had heard when Baruch read the scroll in the hearing of the people.

So all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to say to Baruch, "Bring the scroll you read in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they had heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear and said to Baruch, "We must report all this to the king."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, please, how did you write all these words? Did they come from his own mouth?"

versions.text: Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you come to write all these words? Was it at his dictation?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is a single question with the polite particle נָא ('please'), and מִפִּיו literally means 'from his mouth.' Splitting it into two questions adds content not in the text; the revised wording keeps one question while remaining natural for reading aloud.

text: Baruch answered, "He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."
Then the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are."
After storing the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, they went to the king in the courtyard and reported everything to him.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he brought it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside him.
It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter quarters with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

Each time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns, the king would cut them off with a scribe's knife and throw them into the fire in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire.
Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did any of them tear their clothes.
Even when Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
Instead the king ordered Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll containing the words Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And say concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, 'Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals from it?'
Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: "He will have no one to sit on David's throne; his body will be thrown out, exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.

versions.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on David's throne; his body will be thrown out, exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.
versions.explanation: The divine speech that begins here runs through verse 31, which closes with a quotation mark. An opening quotation mark is needed here for consistency, otherwise the punctuation is unbalanced and a reader (or oral reader) cannot tell where the LORD's words begin.

text: I will punish him and his offspring and his servants for their guilt, and I will bring on them, on the people of Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah every disaster I pronounced against them, because they would not listen."

So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and as Jeremiah dictated, he wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.
